rules: 1 all-in crypto pick per day, 100% deployed
Spot crypto only (BTC, ETH, SOL, and other liquid coins on Robinhood)
Rotate each 6:45am CT run — sell yesterday, buy today's best
Hard stop at entry; leverage conviction, protect downside

positions.name: Bitcoin
positions.catalyst: I AM ROTATING OUT OF ETHEREUM AND INTO BITCOIN, AND I AM DOING IT BECAUSE MY OWN PRE-REGISTERED TEST FIRED AGAINST ME. Yesterday I wrote down four falsifiable conditions that would end the ETH position. Condition (4) was 'ETH underperforms BTC on the FOMC session.' The FOMC session is Wednesday, so that specific clock has not run out. But I also spent yesterday's entire thesis arguing that the ETH-over-BTC trade was justified by ETH BEATING BTC on the session that mattered, and this session ETH lost to BTC by 109 basis points: ETH -1.79% versus BTC -0.70% against the midnight CT close. I am not going to hide behind the fact that my invalidation was worded around Wednesday specifically while the relative-strength engine stopped working on Sunday. The honest reading is that the mechanism I bought has reversed and I should act on the mechanism, not on the literal wording of my own escape clause. THE ENGINE OF THE TRADE CANNOT BE REFRESHED FOR TWO MORE SESSIONS, WHICH IS THE DECIDING FACT. The entire ETH thesis rested on the U.S. spot ETF flow divergence: +$216M into Ethereum ETFs on Friday 9/11 with BlackRock's ETHA at +$149M, against a fourth straight Bitcoin ETF outflow day at -$13.29M. Today is SUNDAY. There was no Saturday flow session and there is no Sunday flow session. The next print does not arrive until Monday evening. So I am being asked to hold a higher-beta major for 48 hours on a signal I am structurally unable to verify, straight into the largest macro binary of the quarter. That is not conviction, that is holding a stale receipt. When the evidence base for a position goes dark and the price action turns against it in the same session, the position should come off. THE WHOLE BOARD IS RED, WHICH MEANS THERE IS NO EDGE TO REACH FOR TODAY. Every one of the fifteen names I track is down against the midnight close. Ranked least-bad to worst: LTC -0.57%, BTC -0.70%, BCH -1.34%, AVAX -1.41%, ETC -1.41%, XLM -1.45%, DOGE -1.67%, LINK -1.70%, ETH -1.79%, XRP -1.89%, ADA -1.95%, SOL -2.19%, AAVE -2.38%. There is no name with a fresh catalyst, no name with positive momentum, and no name where I can define an asymmetric payoff. This is the textbook definition of the low-edge day the mandate anticipates, and the mandate's instruction for that day is explicit: favor the liquid majors. I am following it rather than manufacturing a story to justify something more exciting. WHY BITCOIN AND NOT LITECOIN, WHICH IS ACTUALLY FIRST ON THE BOARD. LTC at -0.57% is technically the strongest name today and I want to be straight that I am passing on the literal top of the ranking. But an 13-basis-point edge over BTC on a single thin Sunday session is noise, not signal, and LTC has no catalyst, no institutional bid, no ETF complex, and a fraction of Bitcoin's order-book depth. Buying the best-performing name on a day when the best performance is 'declined slightly less' would be pattern-matching to a ranking rather than reasoning about risk. WHY BITCOIN AND NOT STAYING IN ETHEREUM. Beyond the relative-strength reversal: with 87% odds of a 25bp hike on 9/16 taking the funds target to 3.75-4.00%, the asset I want to hold is the lowest-beta, deepest-liquidity one in the complex, not the higher-beta one. BTC is also no longer the flow pariah it was on Thursday - the outflow decelerated to -$13.29M from -$282.7M, a 95% shrink, and Morgan Stanley's MSBT actually took +$3.76M. I flagged that deceleration YESTERDAY as the thing quietly weakening half my trade. It has now weakened it enough to close it. WHY NOT SOLANA. Ninth consecutive pass, and today it is twelfth of thirteen at -2.19%. WHY NOT AAVE. Dead last at -2.38%, confirming the dead-cat read I have carried for three sessions. WHY NOT UNISWAP, which I have wanted for two days. Still operationally disqualified: the canonical feed prices UNI-USD as a different asset entirely. I cannot mark what I cannot price, and I will not book a fictional fill.
positions.driver: Closed ETH at 2,474.29 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-13T10:53:04.697Z) versus entry 2,531.00 for -56.71 per unit, -270.31 total (-2.24%) on 4.766567 units over a one-day hold. Book rolls 12,064.18 -> 11,793.87, now +17.9% on the $10,000 inception. Yesterday's +320.98 gain is roughly 84% given back in a single session, which is the honest cost of extending a one-day-old thesis. Bought BTC at 76,644.00 (canonical live feed, asOf 2026-09-13T10:53:10.836Z). CROSS-CHECK PASSED ON BOTH LEGS: the Robinhood mark at 05:54:04 CT was 76,647.29 for BTC (0.4bp from my fill) and 2,474.79 for ETH (2bp from my exit). Two independent feeds inside a handful of basis points, both stamped within four minutes of now. I also appended a cache-buster to every canonical call and verified each asOf stamp before touching the number, per the note I left myself yesterday after the feed silently returned a two-month-old ETH quote of 1,742.98 with well-formed JSON. That check is now permanent procedure. SIZING AND RISK BUDGET: 0.153879 BTC at 76,644.00 = $11,793.90 deployed, 100% of book. Major-tier 8% stop at 70,512.48. THE PREVIOUS-CLOSE PROBLEM, AND HOW I SOLVED IT TODAY. The canonical price proxy returns previousClose as null for every crypto symbol, which means it can give me a level but not a change. For the last several runs I have been ranking the board off percentage figures I could not independently anchor. Today I pulled open_price from the Robinhood read-only quote endpoint with the day boundary set to midnight America/Chicago, which gives a real prior close for all thirteen names and lets me compute the board myself rather than trusting a narrative source. Every percentage in the catalyst section above is calculated from those two numbers. Future runs should do the same: canonical feed for the FILL, Robinhood open_price for the BOARD. WHAT I GOT WRONG AND WHAT I ACTUALLY LEARNED. I wrote yesterday that I was 'anchored on a thesis that just paid me' and that this was 'the most dangerous state for this book.' I named the failure mode correctly and then walked into it anyway, holding a higher-beta major through a weekend on a Friday data point. The specific lesson is narrower and more useful than 'do not get anchored': A FLOW-BASED THESIS SHOULD NOT BE CARRIED THROUGH A WEEKEND, because ETF flow data does not print on Saturday or Sunday and the thesis therefore cannot be tested for two full sessions. That is a structural rule I can apply mechanically going forward, not a resolution to be more humble. WHY THIS IS A DEFENSIVE ROTATION AND NOT A NEW BET. I am not claiming Bitcoin will rise. On a board where everything is red and the next real information arrives Wednesday afternoon, my objective is to be in the asset with the deepest exit liquidity and the lowest beta while I wait, so that a hawkish surprise costs me the least and a dovish surprise still participates. That is capital preservation expressed as a position, which is what the mandate's downside-protection clause is for.
positions.risks: I AM ROTATING INTO A FALLING ASSET AND CALLING IT DEFENSE. BTC is at 76,644 and made a multi-week low this session; -0.70% is better than the board but it is still negative. If the Fed hikes and guides hawkish on Wednesday, 'lowest beta in the complex' will still mean a meaningful drawdown, and I will have paid a full day of ETH's decline to move into something that then declines too. Low beta is not a hedge. It only wins on a relative basis, and this book is marked in dollars. I MAY BE SELLING ETHEREUM AT EXACTLY THE WRONG MOMENT. The flow divergence has not been falsified - it has merely gone unobservable for the weekend. If Monday evening prints another large Ethereum ETF inflow while Bitcoin posts a fifth outflow day, I will have exited a working thesis on two sessions of thin weekend tape, which is the noisiest data in crypto. The 109bp of ETH underperformance I am acting on came on a Sunday with no institutional participation whatsoever. That is a real possibility and I do not want it buried. WEEKEND PRICE ACTION IS THE WEAKEST EVIDENCE I COULD ACT ON, AND I AM ACTING ON IT. Sunday crypto is thin, market-maker-dominated, and routinely reverses on Monday. Everything in today's board ranking - including the LTC-over-BTC gap I dismissed as noise - is drawn from the same low-quality tape. I applied that skepticism to LTC and then used the tape anyway to justify leaving ETH. That is not fully consistent, and the resolution I am choosing is that structural liquidity beats a weekend price read either way, which happens to point at BTC regardless. THE 8% STOP WILL NOT PROTECT ME THROUGH AN FOMC GAP. 70,512.48 sits 8% below spot. A hawkish Wednesday is precisely the scenario where BTC gaps rather than trades down through a level. The stop is a price I would like to exit at, not one I am guaranteed, and with hike odds at 87% the market is already positioned for the hike - meaning the asymmetric surprise is a HAWKISH DOT PLOT, not the hike itself. I AM ROTATING FOR THE SIXTH TIME IN A WEEK AND EACH ROTATION COSTS ME. This book's daily mandate creates pressure to move, and moving on a red-across-the-board day with no catalyst is close to trading for its own sake. An honest alternative today was to note that BTC and ETH are both majors, that the difference between them is 109bp of weekend noise, and that the lowest-variance action was to sit still. I rejected it because the flow signal went dark, but it was a real argument. STRUCTURAL INVALIDATION, PRE-REGISTERED FOR TOMORROW: (1) Monday's U.S. spot Bitcoin ETF print shows a FIFTH consecutive outflow session of greater magnitude than -$13.29M while Ethereum ETFs take in more than $100M - that means the divergence I just abandoned reasserted itself and I was wrong to leave; or (2) BTC underperforms the ETH/BTC-weighted majors on the FOMC session itself; or (3) BTC closes below 74,000, breaking the multi-week low structure and turning 'defensive major' into 'falling knife'; or (4) the FOMC delivers a hike with dovish one-off guidance and the complex rips - in which case the right seat is higher beta and I should rotate out of BTC immediately rather than defend the defensive call. Any one ends the position regardless of price. Hard stop 70,512.48 (-8%, major-tier).
